articles.title: Peach Vortex

From a distance: Reads as a loud pink, violet and orange blob-spot field with a darker brown-tan heart; the dots survive as a polka-dot or petri-dish look. articles.title: Ruby Vortex
articles.summary: Deep crimson-to-magenta marbled swirls with fine sparkle, satin sheen, dark and rich overall. Reads as a deep ruby red with a gritty sparkle; the dark swirl is a subtle shadow and the rest is an even red.
articles.what: Ruby Vortex gradient blend Up close: Raspberry-crimson paint covered in fine 2-3 px grain, with a soft three-armed darker oxblood vortex about 250 px wide near the centre, and a few orange-gold specks creeping in at the corners. The vortex edge is only a change in speckle density, not a line. From a distance: Reads as a deep ruby red with a gritty sparkle; the dark swirl is a subtle shadow and the rest is an even red. Measured spec (average): metal 117, roughness 117, coat 123. Shine: satin. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, sides.
Fits: gt / sports car, show car, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Ruby Vortex" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood and roof: the soft vortex lands in the centre as a subtle accent
Sides: the dark swirl appears once on the door, check the preview
White and yellow numbers read well; dark and red numbers get lost in the grain.
Almost nothing needed: graphics sit well, it is mostly a base
Pairs well with: black, chrome, gold, white.
pitfalls: Not marbled swirls: the old card says marble swirls from crimson to magenta, the render is fine grain with one soft dark triple swirl
Not a Rose Gold: same spec numbers, but a red base with a darker centre vortex rather than a pink to gold fade
Avoid: dark numbers over dark crimson, next to other busy swirl finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 117 (pearl-level metal), roughness 117 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 123 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: dark numbers over dark crimson, next to other busy swirl finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: almost nothing needed: graphics sit well, it is mostly a base; simple stripes and shapes in white, black or gold: a strong red base takes them
Patterns to avoid: other glitter finishes: grain on grain; big swirl patterns that compete with the vortex
Spec overlays that work: none heavy: sparkle is maxed; gloss clearcoat spec to deepen the ruby
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
